title: TACOS: Terrain-Aware COntact Supervision for Visual Footstep Planning; submitted: 2026-10-27; categories: cs.RO, cs.CV; authors: Jean-Michel Fortin; William Larrivée-Hardy; Gabriel Jeanson; Olivier Gamache; Daniele De Martini; François Pomerleau; Philippe Giguère; abstract: Humans navigate their environment based on their vision system, anticipating how the ground will respond before committing to a step. Self-supervised learning could provide legged robots the same ability, but the supervisory signal is typically chosen on intuition, and its effect on what the model learns is rarely examined. We present Terrain-Aware COntact Supervision (TACOS), which proposes a meaningful and consistent footstep instability score, based on the residual of a factor graph in legged state estimation. It projects the continuous score into preceding images to supervise a dense visual predictor. We propose two variants, a hard score that exploits hindsight and a causal soft score available immediately.
